# AXI-to-segmented-memory DMA project
Implement every file and module in output_contract.json. Read the unchanged original README and declaration-only interfaces. Only the selected independent design and its complete RTL closure are requested; unrelated repository components and FPGA board designs are separate designs. Rising clk edges and synchronous active-high rst apply throughout. Assert reset initially for several clocks. Transfer ready/valid signals only on a rising edge with both asserted; preserve data while stalled. Internal state encoding and buffering may differ, but externally visible data, completion and error semantics must match. Private scoring uses one complete usable upstream testbench per point; vectors inside a bench are not additional points. The original source is withheld. Curator clarifications below supplement the original documents and take precedence where explicitly correcting ambiguity.

Implement dma_if_axi integrating dma_if_axi_rd and dma_if_axi_wr. This independent design lives in the PCIe components repository but its public bus is AXI; no PCIe endpoint, FPGA vendor primitive or board wrapper is requested.

- Each read descriptor gives AXI byte address, RAM select, RAM byte address, byte length and tag. Transfer the exact AXI byte interval to the selected segmented RAM destination and report the original tag with zero error on success. Each write descriptor transfers the converse RAM byte interval to AXI. Preserve neighboring bytes on both sides. Address alignment may differ between AXI and RAM.
- The RAM bus is divided into RAM_SEG_COUNT independent ready/valid segments. Segment n's command select/address/data/byte-enables occupy slice n of the packed ports, with segment 0 least significant. A RAM line has RAM_SEG_COUNT*RAM_SEG_BE_WIDTH bytes: a byte address determines line address and byte lane/segment in increasing little-endian order. Total RAM width is twice AXI data width, at least two segments, eight-bit bytes and power-of-two segment byte width. RAM_SEG_ADDR_WIDTH excludes line byte-offset bits. Each write segment waits for ready and tracks ram_wr_done before declaring the descriptor complete. Each read response is accepted via its corresponding response valid/ready; command and response channels can stall independently.
- IMM_ENABLE plus descriptor imm_en selects immediate write data instead of RAM reads. imm is little-endian byte data; write exactly len bytes, with supported immediate length bounded by IMM_WIDTH/8. Other writes read the segmented RAM normally.
- AXI bursts are full-width INCR, obey maximum length and 4-KiB splitting, use proper unaligned first/last strobes and preserve data under backpressure. aw/arburst=01, lock=0, cache=0011, prot=010 and size=log2(AXI bytes). AXI IDs may distinguish pending operations when USE_AXI_ID is enabled; otherwise emit zero IDs. Returned responses must be associated with their pending work.
- read_enable/write_enable gate new descriptors independently. Descriptor status valid is a completion pulse without ready, retaining the supplied tag; errors 0/4/5/6/7 mean success/read-SLVERR/read-DECERR/write-SLVERR/write-DECERR. status_busy indicates outstanding work. Statistics ports report operation and constituent AXI-request start/finish events, lengths/status and internal operation tags, plus table-full/stall; they are diagnostics, and private tests do not claim independent coverage of all counters.
- The scored configuration uses 64-bit AXI data, 16-bit AXI/RAM addresses, two 64-bit RAM segments, 8-bit IDs/tags, immediate writes enabled with 64-bit immediate data, 256 operation entries, read AXI IDs disabled and write AXI IDs enabled. Preserve declared parameters/defaults for compilation. Three complete upstream benches cover integration, read engine and write engine with independent idle/backpressure and unaligned byte transfers. Other PCIe repository designs are outside this closure.

Original-document scope: README describes the independent DMA interface, RAM segmentation and architecture. Exact descriptor, handshake, byte-lane and completion semantics above are curator clarifications reviewed against pinned RTL. The source's parameter assertion blocks are omitted from normalized RTL; synthesizable initialization of operation-table arrays is retained. A reset is still required before work.

Simulation I/O, delays, force/release, final blocks and external includes are forbidden. Constant elaboration functions ($clog2, $unsigned, $signed, $bits) and synthesizable storage initialization are permitted. Save all RTL under the exact required paths; only those files are collected.
